instructions: Wipe the mushrooms clean with a damp paper towel and trim the stem ends. Halve them, or quarter any big ones.
Smash 4 of the garlic cloves with the flat of a knife and peel them. Mince the other 2 cloves. Chop 2 tbsp of the parsley.

Add the oil and the smashed garlic to a large skillet off the heat, then set it over medium-low heat. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, pressing the garlic now and then, until it's golden all over and the oil smells of garlic. Don't let it go dark brown, or the oil turns bitter.
Lift out the smashed garlic and throw it away. Turn the heat up to high.
Add the mushrooms in one layer and leave them alone for about 3 minutes, until the undersides are brown. Don't stir them yet.
Sprinkle the 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper over them. Cook, stirring now and then, for 4 to 5 minutes, until they're golden all over and the liquid in the pan has cooked off.
Add the minced garlic and stir for about 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant. Take the pan off the heat.
Scatter the parsley over the mushrooms. Serve hot in the pan with the bread.
method_notes: This follows RecipeTin Eats; its 4.76 from 137 ratings is for the whole card of five tapas the garlic mushrooms sit in, not for this one recipe alone. RecipeTin Eats and Tara's Multicultural Table both brown the mushrooms in plenty of olive oil and add chopped garlic only at the end so it doesn't burn, finished with parsley. RecipeTin Eats first cooks smashed garlic slowly in the oil to flavor it, Tara's Multicultural Table adds white wine, and Spices Inc adds sherry, lemon, smoked paprika and chili flakes. This keeps to the lead's garlic oil method with no wine, and serves it with bread as Spices Inc does.
